title: Listening & Reading
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata tempat dan kegiatan di waktu luang serta cara membuat dan menanggapi ajakan.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 59-61
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to understand and identify additional key vocabulary about fun activities.
Learners will listen and understand people talking about fun activities.
Learners will read and understand a text about a birthday party.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”

Review the previous lesson with a quick invitation chain: the teacher invites one student (e.g. “Let’s go to the food court!”), the student accepts or refuses politely and then invites another classmate using a different invitation form.
Continue the chain with 5-6 students, encouraging them to use the places and activities from Student Book page 57.
Other alternatives to warm up the class: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at the pictures in Listening A on Student Book page 59.
Tell them that they need to listen and circle the vocabulary word that they hear in the audio.

Before listening, practice pronunciation of the words in task A. The teacher says the two vocabulary choices given for each number, e.g. “Number 1. a. the movie theater. b. the sports center”, and students repeat them aloud.
Play audio 7.3. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check students’ understanding.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner, play the audio again, and then check the answers together (1. a, 2. a, 3. b, 4. b, 5. a, 6. b).

Play audio 7.3 again and ask students to write down the sentences they hear in their notebooks (this is a simple dictation activity). Then show the audio script and ask students to correct their sentences.
This activity is for pronunciation practice.

Play audio 7.4 and encourage students to repeat the words loudly: the movie theater, play badminton, go jogging, invite friends over, play volleyball, go swimming. Encourage them to try to copy the intonation they hear in the audio.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc.
In order to make vocabulary drilling more interesting, students could be guided to act out each activity while they say it (e.g. pretend to hit a shuttlecock for “play badminton”).
Ask students to look at listening task C and read the activities in column A together.

Tell students that they need to listen and circle True if the activity they hear is the same as the activity in column A. If it is different, they circle False and write the activity they hear in column B.
Play audio 7.5. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to do the task. Then, continue with the audio.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner, then play the audio again.
Check the answers together and write them on the board (1. False – go to the movie theater, 2. True, 3. True, 4. False – go jogging, 5. False – play volleyball, 6. False – go swimming).
If there is time, show the audio script and ask students to read the sentences aloud in pairs, paying attention to their intonation.
Ask students to look at the pictures on Student Book page 60-61.
Ask the class, “What can you see on the page?” and some specific questions about the pictures, for example, “How many people can you see?”, “What are they doing?”
Giving some personal questions is also suggested to make it more relatable to students, for example, “Have you ever been to a birthday party with a special theme?”
Ask students to look at task A on Student Book page 60 and discuss what they can see in the pictures, in pairs.

Practice pronunciation of the words in task A. The teacher says the two vocabulary choices given for each number, e.g. “Number 1. a. make costumes. b. attend a festival”, and students repeat them aloud.
Ask students to work together in pairs to circle the words that match each picture.
Check the answers as a class (1. a, 2. b, 3. b, 4. a) and drill the key vocabulary again: make costumes, take photos, play VR games, watch a movie.
Ask students to look at task B on Student Book page 60.

Put students in pairs and ask them to discuss the questions, e.g. “What do you like to do for your birthday?”, “Where would you like to have your birthday party?”, “Are there any special foods you like to eat on your birthday?”
Give students 3-5 minutes to complete the task.

Then ask some students to share their answers with the class. Answers will vary because these questions require students' own personal responses, and it’s not important if students can’t answer fully in English yet.
Tell students that they will listen and read the birthday party invitation. Play audio 7.6 and ask them to read the text silently.
Next, play audio 7.6 again and ask students to read the text aloud, following the audio. Ask if there are any questions about the language in the text.

As a way to make the reading session more engaging, teachers could divide the class into several groups and assign each group to read one part of the invitation alternately in different ways (e.g. excited or whispering).
Ask students to look at task D on Student Book page 61.
Tell students they will read through the invitation again and circle yes or no for each statement based on the invitation.
The first question can be done together as a class to make sure students know what to do. Then, they can complete the task in pairs or by themselves.
Ask students to check their answers with a friend.
Check the answers as a class and write them on the board (1. yes, 2. no, 3. no, 4. yes, 5. yes). Ask students to show where they found the information in the text.
For number 6, answers will vary. Ask some students to explain why they would or wouldn’t like to go to the party.
Now ask students to look at task E.

Instruct them to discuss the questions in groups of three or four students, e.g. “When is your birthday?”, “Do you usually celebrate your birthday? How?”, “Describe a birthday party you would like to have: the theme, activities, and food.”
Encourage students to use the vocabulary from this unit in their answers, e.g. “I want a costume party. We can make costumes and take photos.”
After about 6-8 minutes, elicit some answers for each question from each group.
This activity could be done if there is more time.
Ask students to make an invitation for their own birthday party on a blank piece of paper.

The invitation should include the date, the location, the activities they want to do at the party (e.g. play VR games, watch a movie, take photos), and present ideas. Remind students to use invitation forms such as “Would you like to come to my party?” or “Let’s celebrate together!”
Give students around 10-15 minutes. They should write the text first, and then if they have time, they can illustrate their invitation.
After students have finished, ask them to walk around the classroom and show their invitations to each other. Classmates can accept or refuse the invitation politely.
This could be done as a homework task if there isn’t enough time during the lesson.
Wrap up the class by asking 1-2 students what fun activity they would like to do at their next birthday party, and who they would invite.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: ketepatan jawaban tugas listening (menomori/menjodohkan/melengkapi).
Pertanyaan pemahaman bacaan (literal & inferensial) dan pembahasan bersama.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
